entities.summary: Detlef Lienau was a German architect born in Holstein. He is credited with having introduced the French style to American building construction, notably the mansard roof and all its decorative flourishes. Trained at the École des Beaux-Arts, Paris, he designed virtually every type of Victorian structure—cottages, mansions, townhouses, apartment houses, hotels, tenements, banks, stores, churches, schools, libraries, offices, factories, railroad stations, and a museum. Lienau was recognized by clients and colleagues alike as one of the most creative and technically proficient architects of the period, and was one of the 29 founding members of the American Institute of Architects.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Detlef Lienau's introduction of French style architecture to American building construction had a significant regional impact, influencing the design of over 100 types of buildings across the United States. His work at the École des Beaux-Arts, Paris, and his membership in the American Institute of Architects, demonstrate his lasting influence on American architectural history.
